(1) the multicast capacity can be achieved by allowing information mixing only on edges entering relay vertices, (2) the multicast capacity is achieved by routing and network coding, and (3) the cut bound is achievable by routing.
the multicast capacity of a network can be achieved by allowing mixing on edges entering only a set of special nodes, and that the special nodes can be identified by a simple algorithm.
the multicast capacity is achieved by routing and network coding, and that routing and network coding can be combined to achieve the multicast capacity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two main questions: (1) what are the necessary and sufficient conditions for achieving the cut bound by performing network coding on edges entering relay (or destination) nodes?
the following questions: (1) What is the multicast capacity for networks that allow routing, but not network coding?
the following question: How can the multicast capacity of a network be achieved?

, given a network with a single source and multiple destinations, if the network is hardwired, then the multicast capacity can be achieved by network coding, and if all nodes other that the source are destinations and the network is not hardwired, the multicast capacity can also be achieved by network routing.
network coding can be used to replace routing in all cases, including the case where routing works.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a unifying framework to study network information flows, and that our framework is useful in proving theorems for network coding and routing.

The main takeaway from our work is that
network coding and routing are special cases of the same general principle: information mixing on edges entering nodes.
